data.title: Canada Wholesale Sales Rise 0.3% in July
data.description:
By Robb M. Stewart

OTTAWA--Canadian wholesale trade was buoyed in July by a rise in sales of metal products.

Wholesale sales rose 0.3% from the month before to a seasonally adjusted 93.09 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of US$66.96 billion, Statistics Canada said Tuesday. That was stronger than the data agency's advance estimate of sales retreating 0.6% for the month, and builds on the 2.8% rise a month earlier.

Compared with a year earlier, sales climbed 7.9%. And in volume terms, sales were down 0.6% during July but up 1.8% compared with a year prior.

The result contrasts with a pullback in manufacturing shipments in July and drop in monthly sales volumes, which points to headwinds for the economy to kick off the third quarter.

Sales were up in three of the seven wholesale industries tracked by Statistics Canada, which representeed half of all sector trade during the month. The biggest increase was in building materials and supplies, driven by sales by metal service centers on the back of higher steel products prices.

Sales by food, drink and tobacco wholesalers also were up for the month, led by increased food industry volumes.

Weakness in mineral, ore and precious metal sales moderated the advance for the sector, due in part to lower sales volumes of precious metals.

The value of inventories held by wholesalers in Canada was essentially unchanged for the month at C$140.65 billion, though stocks were up 5.5% on a year earlier.

Wholesalers--the largest component of Canada's services sector--connect farmers or manufacturers that produce goods with the companies and public institutions that use them. They also import goods from other countries and redistribute them within Canada.

Manufacturing trade weakened in July, with sales falling 0.4% from a month earlier following five straight months of rising activity. In volume terms, factory sales were down a sharper 1.4% for the months though up 0.4% year-over-year.

Statistics Canada previously estimated gross domestic product was essentially unchanged in July, following three consecutive months of growth for the economy. In annualized terms, the economy expanded 3.3% in the second quarter, the strongest growth in three years.

Including sales by petroleum, oilseed and grain merchants, wholesale trade for July was up 0.4% at C$137.3 billion, and 13.8% higher than in the same month last year. Inventories on the same basis were 0.6% higher than in June at C$154.96 billion.

data.title: Broker’s call: CDSL (Buy)
data.description:
Target: ₹1,620

CMP: ₹1,311

After a soft FY26, in which revenue growth decelerated to 5.8 per cent y-o-y (vs 3Y CAGR of 27 per cent) and EBITDA margin contracted about 651 bps to 51.2 per cent, we believe Central Depository Services (CDSL) is at the cusp of a volume-led growth recovery.

The two key headwinds are now behind. The pricing cuts in transaction charges and KYC (create and fetch), which dented KYC blended realisations by about 8-10 per cent, are fully in the base, and the heavy phase of technology and regulatory-led spending has largely played out. Primary market activity has turned decisively, with 50 mainboard IPOs in Q2-FY27 vs nine in Q1-FY27, and BO account additions have recovered to 1 lakh/day from a trough of 70K/day in March 2026.

We expect about 1 crore new accounts in Q2-FY27E (58 lakh in Q1FY27), the best quarterly addition in eight quarters. This should revive transaction revenue (almost flat for five quarters), KYC revenue and IPO/corporate action income (+18 per cent y-o-y in FY27E vs -1.9 per cent in FY26), while a widening issuer base compounds the annual issuer charge annuity (around 40 per cent of revenue).

The stock has underperformed over the past one year and is presently trading at a 42x FY28E which is about 7 per cent discount to its historical five-year average one-year forward P/E multiple of 45x.

This, in our view, prices in the FY26 slowdown but not the recovery. We upgrade CDSL to Buy from Add with a target price of ₹1,620, based on 45x Sep-28E EPS, in line with the 45-55x band the stock has commanded in previous growth-recovery phases.

data.title: Goldman's Panic Index logged third-largest daily drop in 3 years
data.description:
A sudden three-point drop in the Goldman Sachs Panic Index on Friday wiped out broad market fear, registering as the third-largest single-day decline in the past three years.

The collapse in panic left markets entering the weekend with much less fear priced into broader indexes , alongside continued market dispersion and recently rebuilt long positions in the tech sector . With generalized anxiety fading, investor attention shifted toward emerging headlines surrounding artificial intelligence and the Middle East war.

Broad market volatility also remained muted, with the CBOE Volatility Index staying well under 20 and sitting at roughly 16.90 at the time of writing.

Meanwhile, major stock indexes are extending last week's losses so far this week due to a mix of tech sector drops, energy spikes and bond market pressures. AI and chipmaker shares retreated after prominent tech CEOs called for a slowdown and tighter pacing in AI development. Elsewhere, crude oil prices climbed further above $100 a barrel after Middle East attacks and critical pipeline shutdowns in Saudi Arabia worsened supply fears. Adding to the market strain, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield hit the key 5% threshold ahead of a Federal Reserve decision on Wednesday, which is largely expected to feature a rate hike.

data.title: Boxlight Expands STEM Education Partnership with Jefferson Parish Schools
data.description:
Boxlight Corporation (Nasdaq: BOXL), a leading provider of integrated education technology solutions, today announced the expansion of its STEM education partnership with Jefferson Parish Schools in Louisiana, providing more than 200 Robo E4 3D printers, filament, and MyStemKits curriculum access for science teachers across the district.

The initiative began with the district exploring approximately 50 3D printers for its middle and high school science programs. Through discovery conversations, the project expanded as district leaders identified a need for more than hardware; they were looking for curriculum, professional development, implementation planning, ongoing support, and a true technology partner.

The Robo E4 printer was selected not only because it is a high-speed machine designed for the rigors of the classroom, but also because it comes bundled with MimioSTEM’s award-winning curriculum solution: MyStemKits. This curriculum platform provides standards-driven lessons, activities, design challenges, and ready-to-print 3D models designed to help educators integrate hands-on STEM learning into instruction and make sure that their new 3D printers can be used to their fullest potential.

“We are grateful to Boxlight for investing in our teachers and students in a way that goes beyond simply providing new technology. These resources will give our students more opportunities to create, explore, solve problems and bring what they are learning to life.” Dr. James Gray, Superintendent, Jefferson Parish Schools “Our teachers will also have the training, curriculum and support they need to bring these learning experiences into the classroom. When teachers feel prepared and supported, students have more opportunities to engage, grow and see what is possible through STEM.”

Aligning Technology with Instruction

Boxlight worked with district leaders to align MyStemKits resources with Jefferson Parish’s science scope and sequence, helping ensure teachers have relevant instructional materials from the start of implementation.

“In Jefferson Parish Schools, our focus is always on making sure new resources connect directly to what students are learning every day. By aligning the technology with our science curriculum, teachers can introduce hands-on experiences that reinforce key concepts and give students new ways to demonstrate what they know.” - Laura Roussel, Chief Academic Officer, Jefferson Parish Schools.

During that process, Boxlight identified a need for additional environmental science content and developed new lessons to help address those instructional gaps, demonstrating the company’s commitment to supporting district-specific instructional needs.

Jefferson Parish Schools selected Bluum as its reseller to meet the district’s procurement requirements through TIMS. Bluum provided significant support throughout the sales process, including local district engagement, site visits, product demonstrations, and planning and procurement support.

“Jefferson Parish Schools had a clear vision for expanding hands-on STEM learning, and we were proud to support the district as the project evolved from an initial technology discussion into a comprehensive instructional initiative,” said Kurt Roberts, Client Director, Bluum. “Working alongside Boxlight, we were able to help connect the district with the technology, curriculum, professional learning, and support needed to make the implementation successful.”

Professional Development and Ongoing Support

Boxlight developed an implementation roadmap that includes teacher training, curriculum integration, ongoing coaching, and continued support throughout the school year.

The rollout will include a customized week-long professional development program in September, with multiple Boxlight team members traveling to New Orleans to provide concurrent sessions tailored to teachers’ specific subjects and grade levels.

In addition to the kick-off week of professional learning, Boxlight will also provide various virtual learning follow-up sessions for interested educators and has provided a 3D printer certification course so that both the teachers and their students can become 3D printer certified.

The initiative reflects Boxlight’s approach to education technology: providing the technology, curriculum, training, and ongoing support needed to turn classroom tools into meaningful instructional experiences.

Jefferson Parish Schools leaders emphasized the importance of communication, curriculum support, product support, and professional learning throughout the planning process. Boxlight’s comprehensive support model is designed to help teachers confidently integrate 3D printing into instruction and use it to engage students in hands-on STEM learning.

“This initiative is a strong example of how understanding a district’s goals can transform a technology purchase into a broader instructional partnership,” said Jillian Dale, STEM Sales Manager, Boxlight. “Our goal is to make it easier for educators to confidently use technology to support curriculum and create meaningful learning experiences.”

About Jefferson Parish Schools: Jefferson Parish Schools is the largest and most diverse public school system in Louisiana. Our system of 74 schools serves approximately 45,000 students on both banks of the Mississippi River. With approximately 6,000 employees, JP Schools is one of the largest employers in Jefferson Parish. Our district exists to provide the education our students deserve to succeed in life and make our world a better place.

About Boxlight Corporation

Boxlight Corporation (Nasdaq: BOXL) is a leading provider of education technology solutions through its award-winning Clevertouch®, FrontRow™, Mimio®, and Boxlight brands. The company develops, sells, and supports a portfolio of instructional software, interactive displays, classroom audio, campus communication, emergency notification, digital signage, STEM solutions, and professional services designed to improve engagement, communication, collaboration, and safety in learning environments worldwide.

For more information about Boxlight and its solutions, visit www.boxlight.com.

(12:31 GMT) *JD Sports Fashion Names Mike Grimes as Group Chief Marketing Officer
(12:32 GMT) *JD Sports Fashion: Appointments Are Effective Immediately
(12:33 GMT) *JD Sports Fashion: Appointments Aim to Capture Significant Growth Opportunity Seen in North America
(12:34 GMT) *JD Sports Fashion: Mersho Replaces John Hall, Who Retired
(13:07 GMT) JD Sports Appoints New Marketing Chief, Americas Boss

By Andrea Figueras

JD Sports Fashion named a new marketing chief and a new leader for its North America division, looking to boost growth and strengthen its presence in the region.

The British retailer named Mike Grimes as group chief marketing officer, who previously worked as marketing boss for the North America business.

The company, which sells brands including Nike and Adidas, also appointed John Mersho as president and chief executive of the North American division. Mersho, who held the role of chief commercial officer for the business since 2025, replaces John Hall, who retired.

The appointments, both with immediate effect, reflect JD's focus on capturing the "significant growth opportunity" it sees in North America, the company said Tuesday. The region is JD's largest market and represented 38% of group sales in fiscal 2026, ended Jan. 31.

"These appointments represent an important step in the next phase of JD's growth," Chief Executive Regis Schultz said Tuesday. "John and Mike are outstanding leaders - both well-tenured within our business, bringing extensive experience and deep knowledge of the markets we operate in."

data.title: Spain Inflation Accelerates As Estimated
data.description:
MADRID (dpa-AFX) - Spain's inflation accelerated to the highest level in more than three years in August, as initially estimated, final data from the statistical office INE showed Tuesday.

Consumer price inflation rose to 4.3 percent, in line with flash estimate, from 3.6 percent in July. The latest figure was the highest since February 2023, when inflation was 6.0 percent.

Meanwhile, EU harmonized inflation advanced more-than-estimated to 4.6 percent from 3.9 percent. The initially estimated inflation was 4.5 percent.

Month-on-month, the consumer price index posted an increase of 0.7 percent, faster than the 0.3 percent rise in July. The August rate matched estimate.

The harmonized index of consumer prices climbed 0.7 percent, slightly faster than the flash estimate of 0.6 percent, and followed a flat growth in July.

data.title: Bulgaria Inflation Confirmed At 5.1%
data.description:
BRUSSELS (dpa-AFX) - Bulgaria's consumer price inflation accelerated as estimated initially in August amid higher transportation costs, the latest data from the National Statistical Institute showed on Tuesday.

The consumer price index, or CPI, climbed 5.1 percent year-over-year in August, faster than the 4.5 percent rise in July. That was in line with the flash data published on August 31.

Inflation based on transportation quickened notably to 21.5 percent from 14.5 percent, and housing and utility costs grew at a stable pace of 5.1 percent. Meanwhile, the annual price growth of food and non-alcoholic beverages eased to 0.6 percent from 1.2 percent, and clothing and footwear prices remained flat.

On a monthly basis, consumer prices rose 0.6 percent after rebounding 0.8 percent in July, confirming the flash data.

The EU measure of inflation, the harmonized index of consumer prices, also rose at a faster pace of 5.1 percent annually in August versus a 4.4 percent increase in July, as estimated.

data.title: UAE's ADNOC buys millions of barrels of Iraqi crude, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • ADNOC trading arm buys Iraqi crude at discounts, sources say
  • ADNOC agrees to buy 72 million barrels for Aug-Sept, source says
  • Other companies also buy crude from Iraq

By Nidhi Verma and Ahmed Rasheed

Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) has bought millions of barrels of discounted crude from Iraq's state oil firm, three people familiar with the matter said, expanding its role as a trader amid supply disruptions from the Iran war.

The state company, through its trading arm, was the biggest lifter of Iraqi crude in August and September, two Iraqi energy sources said, helping boost Iraqi exports that had been severely curtailed in the earlier months of the war.

ADNOC agreed to buy 32 million Iraqi barrels in August at discounts ranging from $24.90 to $27 a barrel, and a further 40 million barrels in September, including 10 million barrels at an $18-a-barrel discount and 30 million barrels at a $25 discount, one of the Iraqi sources said.

The second Iraqi source said that while Iraq's state oil marketing organisation SOMO had allocated ADNOC 32 million barrels in August, the UAE giant lifted 20 million barrels due to export constraints and Basra Oil Company's inability to secure sufficient crude.

ADNOC has lifted 14 million Iraqi barrels so far in September, the person said.

A third source said ADNOC had bought about 20 million barrels of crude from Iraq's state-owned SOMO in tenders at a discount of between $25 and $27 a barrel for September through October lifting.

Other companies are also buying Iraqi crude. SOMO offered August-loading cargoes at steep discounts, drawing in other buyers including Chinese state majors PetroChina and Zhenhua Oil, TotalEnergies , Vitol, Trafigura, Mercuria and Cathay Petroleum, trade sources told Reuters earlier.

Last month, Iran granted permission for a number of tankers carrying Iraqi oil to pass through the Strait of Hormuz following repeated requests from Baghdad through various channels, Iran’s state news agency IRNA reported.

Iraq's exports had been severely curtailed in the earlier months of the war due in part to its location at the top of the Gulf and the lack of its own shipping fleet.

State-owned ADNOC has become more nimble since the war started, using an expanding tanker fleet as well as a pipeline to the port of Fujairah to move oil out of the Gulf and across the Strait of Hormuz.

PUT THE PAST BEHIND THEM

Despite attacks on some ADNOC tankers, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Sunday met with UAE Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi, saying the two sides had agreed to put the past behind them.

Iraq has been exporting about 2 million barrels of oil per day this month according to Kpler data, down from 2.354 million bpd in August but above the 1.374 million bpd in July.

UAE crude exports have risen to 3.236 million bpd this month, up from 2.886 million bpd in August and 2.871 million bpd in July, according to Kpler.

ADNOC plans to process most of the crude purchased from other Gulf producers at its Ruwais refinery and sell more of its own crude into the international market, one of the three sources said.
